q: Where is the Kharan Desert located?
facts: • Kharan is an arid region in western Balochistan.
Do not confuse the Kharan Desert with the Thar or Cholistan deserts.

q: On which continent is Lake Victoria?
facts: • Lake Victoria borders Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
It is a major source region of the White Nile.

q: Which Caliph is most commonly associated with the title Amir-ul-Mu'minin?
ans: Hazrat Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), the second Caliph
facts: • The title means “Commander of the Faithful.”
Hazrat Hamza (RA) was the Prophet's uncle and a martyr of Uhud, not the standard answer to this title.

q: What are Canada's official national sports?
facts: • Canada's National Sports of Canada Act recognizes both sports.
Ice hockey alone is an incomplete answer if the question asks for Canada's official national sports plural.

q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque located?
facts: • The Shah Jahan Mosque is known for its tile work and acoustics.
The Badshahi Mosque, by contrast, is in Lahore.

q: What is the world's largest cold desert?
facts: • A desert is classified mainly by low precipitation, not by heat.
The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Khaybar fought?
ans: Against the Jewish tribes/strongholds of Khaybar in 7 AH (629 CE)
facts: • Khaybar was an oasis north of Madinah.
The battle took place after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah; historical descriptions should avoid treating all Jewish people as a single group.

q: Who wrote “Kashf-ul-Mahjoob”?
ans: Ali ibn Usman al-Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)
facts: • It is one of the earliest major Persian works on Sufism.
The author's shrine is in Lahore.

q: Which organization promotes peaceful nuclear technology and nuclear safeguards?
ans: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), established in 1957; nuclear-test monitoring is a separate CTBTO role
facts: • IAEA headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.
The CTBTO Preparatory Commission develops the international monitoring system for detecting nuclear test explosions; IAEA does not “protect the world from all nuclear explosions.”

q: When was New Delhi inaugurated as the capital of British India?
ans: 13 February 1931; the decision to shift the capital from Calcutta was announced in 1911
facts: • The new imperial capital was ceremonially inaugurated by Viceroy Lord Irwin.
“Delhi to Kolkata” reverses the direction; the capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi/New Delhi.

q: Where is the Flint River located?
facts: • The Flint River flows south through Georgia and joins the Chattahoochee to form the Apalachicola River.
It is unrelated to the Flint River in Michigan, so a state should be specified.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
facts: • Caracas is in northern Venezuela near the Caribbean coast.
The country's official name is the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

q: What is the currency of Cuba?
facts: • Cuba unified its currency system in 2021.
Do not confuse the Cuban peso with the currencies of other Caribbean states.

q: Who was the first permanent president of the All-India Muslim League?
ans: Aga Khan III (elected permanent president in 1908)
facts: • The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka on 30 December 1906.
The early movement sought political representation and safeguards for Muslims in British India.

q: When was the OIC established?
facts: • The organization followed the first Islamic Summit in Rabat in September 1969.
Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 26

q: When did the United Nations officially come into existence?
facts: • The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco.
24 October is observed as United Nations Day. Primary / official reference

q: What does Tanzil mean?
facts: • The word describes the sending down of divine revelation.
“Nazil” means descended or revealed in Urdu usage.

q: “Where is the Amnesty Airport?”
ans: Unclear wording; if “Heathrow Airport” was intended, it is in London, United Kingdom
facts: • The uploaded question appears mistranscribed; “Amnesty Airport” is not a recognized airport name.
Please use the exact original source before memorizing this item.

q: Which countries are separated by the 38th parallel in Korea?
facts: • The 38th parallel was used as a division line after World War II.
The Korean Demilitarized Zone was later established around the armistice line in 1953 and does not follow the parallel exactly everywhere.

q: Who was the leader of the Quraysh opponents at the Battle of Badr commonly named in GK questions?
facts: • The Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH / 624 CE.
Abu Jahl was killed during the battle according to Islamic historical accounts.

q: Which country provided major assistance in building Warsak Dam?
facts: • Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River near Peshawar.
It was commissioned/inaugurated in 1960 and has served irrigation and hydropower purposes. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 28

q: Which Chinese autonomous region borders Pakistan?
facts: • Pakistan and China connect through the Khunjerab Pass.
Xinjiang borders several Central Asian states as well as Pakistan, India and Afghanistan.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan with China?
facts: • Khunjerab lies on the Karakoram Highway at roughly 4,693 m elevation.
It links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.

q: Which city is popularly called the “City of Flowers” in Pakistan?
facts: • Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is also a historic city on routes connecting South Asia with Central Asia.

q: Where is the Shahi Qila (Lahore Fort) located?
facts: • Lahore Fort is part of the Lahore Fort and Shalamar Gardens UNESCO World Heritage property.
The fort's present Mughal form is strongly associated with Akbar and later Mughal emperors.

q: In which city is the National College of Arts (NCA) located?
facts: • NCA is one of Pakistan's oldest art and design institutions.
It also has a campus in Rawalpindi.

q: The Darling River is located in which country?
facts: • The Darling is part of the Murray–Darling river system.
The Murray and Darling are important rivers in southeastern Australia.

q: Who was Pakistan's first Commander-in-Chief of the Army?
facts: • Messervy served from August 1947 to February 1948.
He was succeeded by General Douglas Gracey before Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief in 1951. Primary / official reference

q: What is the fifth pillar of Islam?
ans: Hajj (pilgrimage), for those able to perform it
facts: • The five pillars are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.
Hajj is performed in the Islamic month of Dhul-Hijjah.

q: How many obligatory acts of Hajj are listed in common Hanafi teaching?
ans: Three, in the common Hanafi classification; counts differ by school
facts: • Hanafi lists typically name standing at Arafat, Tawaf al-Ziyarah and the required amount of shaving/cutting hair as obligations (wajibat are a different category).
Always follow the specific fiqh syllabus because “obligations” can mean different categories.

q: In 622 CE, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrated to which city?
facts: • The Hijrah took place in 622 CE.
The event marks the epoch used for the Hijri calendar.

q: Diphtheria primarily affects which part of the body?
ans: The nose and throat/upper respiratory tract; it can also damage the heart and nerves
facts: • Diphtheria is a bacterial disease caused by toxigenic strains of Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
Vaccination with diphtheria toxoid is a key prevention measure.

q: How many Qur'an memorizers were traditionally reported martyred at Yamama?
facts: • The Battle of Yamama occurred during the Ridda Wars under Caliph Abu Bakr (RA).
Reports of the deaths of memorizers are traditionally linked to the later collection of the Qur'an.

q: What is Imam Bukhari's full name/kunya?
ans: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari; kunya Abu Abd Allah
facts: • His major hadith collection is Sahih al-Bukhari.
He was born in Bukhara in 810 CE.

q: Who compiled Sunan Abi Dawud?
ans: Imam Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani
facts: • Sunan Abi Dawud is one of the six major Sunni hadith collections.
Its focus is strongly on narrations relevant to legal rulings.

q: What does the name “Pakistan” mean?
facts: • The name was coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
The word was also devised as an acronym associated with regions of the subcontinent in the original pamphlet “Now or Never.”

q: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of which Companion?
facts: • Aisha (RA) was one of the wives of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
Abu Bakr (RA) became the first Caliph after the Prophet's death.

q: Where is Masjid-e-Nabawi located?
facts: • The mosque was established by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after the Hijrah.
It contains the area of the Prophet's chamber and is one of Islam's holiest mosques.

q: What is another name associated with Bait-ul-Maqdis in Jerusalem?
ans: Al-Aqsa Mosque / the sacred sanctuary in Jerusalem; wording should distinguish the mosque from the wider site
facts: • Masjid al-Aqsa is in the Old City of Jerusalem.
“Bayt al-Maqdis” can refer to the wider sacred place/Jerusalem, not only a single building.

q: In which province is the Thal Desert?
facts: • Thal lies between the Indus and Jhelum rivers.
It includes areas of Bhakkar, Khushab, Layyah, Mianwali and nearby districts.

q: Near which city is the Cholistan Desert commonly associated?
facts: • Cholistan is also called Rohi.
The Derawar Fort is a well-known landmark in the Cholistan region.

q: Which is Pakistan's largest district by area in commonly cited administrative listings?
ans: Chagai District, Balochistan (confirm current boundaries with the latest official list)
facts: • Chagai is in western Balochistan near the borders with Iran and Afghanistan.
District rankings can change when administrative boundaries are revised.

q: In which river are Pakistan's blind dolphins found?
facts: • The Indus river dolphin is a freshwater species with very limited vision.
It uses echolocation to navigate turbid river water.

q: Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan?
ans: The National Assembly, from among its members
facts: • The Prime Minister must command the support of a majority in the National Assembly.
The President is elected by an electoral college that includes Parliament and provincial assemblies.

q: Which Indian Prime Minister visited Pakistan in February 1999?
facts: • The visit was associated with the Lahore Declaration.
The bus journey and talks occurred shortly before the Kargil conflict of 1999.

q: What is the highest military award of Switzerland?
ans: The question is misleading: Switzerland has no conventional national honours/order system; armed-forces service awards do exist
facts: • Swiss tradition restricts national orders and titles, though the military has service and mission awards.
It is not accurate to name a single Swiss equivalent of Pakistan's Nishan-e-Haider without defining the category.

q: What is the full form of ISPR?
facts: • ISPR is the media and public-relations wing of Pakistan's armed forces.
Its role includes communicating official military information and statements.

q: What is 2 + 2 ÷ 2?
facts: • Division is performed before addition under standard order of operations.
Calculate 2 ÷ 2 = 1, then add 2.

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 120?
facts: • One tenth of 120 equals 12; one quarter of 12 equals 3.
This is a two-step fraction question.

q: Manama is the capital of which country?
facts: • Manama is Bahrain's capital and largest city.
Bahrain is an island country in the Persian Gulf.

q: What is the currency of Egypt?
facts: • The Egyptian pound is divided into 100 piastres (qirsh).
Cairo is Egypt's capital.

q: What is the currency of Australia?
facts: • The Australian dollar is used by Australia and several Pacific territories.
Its symbol is commonly A$ or $ depending on context.

q: Which two oceans are connected by the Panama Canal?
facts: • The canal officially opened in 1914.
It links the Atlantic via the Caribbean Sea to the Pacific and greatly shortens shipping routes.

q: When was the World Trade Organization established?
facts: • The WTO succeeded the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) framework.
Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. Primary / official reference

q: In which country is the OIC headquartered?
facts: • The OIC itself was founded in Rabat, Morocco, in 1969.
Headquarters location and founding venue are different facts.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
facts: • Buenos Aires is Argentina's capital and a major port.
Argentina is in the southern part of South America.

q: Who was Pakistan's second Governor-General?
facts: • Muhammad Ali Jinnah was the first Governor-General.
Nazimuddin later served as Pakistan's second Prime Minister.

q: What is the real cube root of unity?
ans: 1; if asking for all cube roots of unity, there are three: 1, ω and ω²
facts: • The equation x³ = 1 has three complex roots.
Only one of them is real: x = 1.

q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed?
facts: • Abu Jahl was a leading opponent of the early Muslims in Mecca.
Badr was fought in 2 AH / 624 CE.

q: The Bay of Biscay lies along which country/countries?
ans: The western coast of France and the northern coast of Spain
facts: • It is part of the northeastern Atlantic Ocean.
The bay is known for rough seas and strong storms.

q: When was the All-India Muslim League founded?
facts: • The original name was All-India Muslim League.
The Lahore Resolution was passed in 1940, fourteen years before independence.

q: Who was the first wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
facts: • Khadijah (RA) was a successful merchant and the first person to accept Islam in the traditional account.
Their marriage preceded the first revelation.

q: Where is the Kirthar Range located?
ans: Along the Sindh–Balochistan region; it is a distinct mountain range, not the Suleiman Range
facts: • The Kirthar National Park is in Sindh.
The Suleiman Range is a separate range farther to the northwest.

q: What is a major sacred site of Sikhism in Pakistan associated with Guru Nanak's birthplace?
facts: • Gurdwara Janam Asthan marks the traditional birthplace of Guru Nanak.
Kartarpur is another major Sikh pilgrimage site associated with his later life.

q: How many languages are spoken in Pakistan?
ans: More than 70 languages are reported; exact counts vary by classification and survey
facts: • Urdu is the national language; English is used widely for official and higher-education purposes.
Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki, Balochi and several others are widely spoken.

q: When was the Simla Conference held?
facts: • The conference aimed to agree on the composition of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
It failed largely over representation and the Muslim League's claim to speak for India's Muslims.

q: Who is Pakistan's Prime Minister as of 14 October 2026?
facts: • Shehbaz Sharif began his current term in March 2024.
The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 43

q: When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur?
facts: • The incident took place in the United Provinces under British rule.
Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement after the violence.

q: What was the religion of the Negus (Najashi) before the traditional account of his acceptance of Islam?
facts: • Najashi was the ruler of Abyssinia (often identified with the Aksumite kingdom).
He gave protection to early Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia.

q: How many Muslims fought at the Battle of Badr in the common traditional count?
ans: About 313 (some reports give slightly different figures)
facts: • Badr occurred in 2 AH / 624 CE.
Muslim force totals vary slightly across traditional reports; 313 is the standard GK answer.

q: Who is widely credited with founding the Indian National Congress?
ans: Allan Octavian Hume, together with Indian leaders
facts: • The Congress was founded in 1885.
Its first session was held in Bombay (now Mumbai), with Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee as president.

q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
facts: • The first session met in Bombay in December 1885.
A.O. Hume was a key organizer, but the organization involved Indian leaders too.
